_readme: ТЗ §30 rules, enforced by Sarko.Loot.RealLootTablesObeyTheDesignRules: junk may be empty <=15%, common <=8%, med <=15%, good and military NEVER empty. med yields no weapons and no vehicle parts. Item ids must exist in Data/Items/items.json or the file fails to load. VEHICLE PARTS: the rule used to be 'singles at <=3% of their tier's weight'. It has been replaced deliberately (spec §6), not relaxed by accident. 3% was protecting against 'the bicycle in one raid' and it overshot by a mile: Monte-Carlo over 20 000 careers on the real table put the bicycle at a MEDIAN OF 30 RAIDS, p90 67, with wheel_small (weight 1/103, needed twice, qty {1,1}) as the bottleneck — three to seven hours to the only stated goal. military.bike_frame is 5, military.wheel_small is 8 with qty {1,2}, and chain is in military at 4; re-simulated that is median 6 raids, p90 11, first part typically in raid 1-2. The rule the test now enforces is the one that was actually meant: no tier hands out MORE THAN ONE of a part per container roll on average, and the whole map's expected yield of any single part stays under one per raid, so a bicycle can never be a one-raid event. good.chain stays at 2 — the good tier is not a parts faucet and military is. CLOTHING: `jacket` was in the catalog and in NO loot table, so the clothing slot could only ever be filled by a debug exec — the slot was unfillable by playing, which is a slot that does not exist. It is in `good` at weight 3, one under the backpack it sits beside: a scavenged coat is a decent find and not a military one, and `good` is the tier the map puts on the route rather than at the far end of it. It is also one of the four server-authored ВИЛАЗКА kits (sarko-api domain.SortieKits, the `patched` and `provisioned` rows), so the recovery path can hand one out too. Neither affects the vehicle-part ceiling below: a jacket is `gear`, and ADDING weight to a tier can only lower that tier's parts share.
